request.spec:
A person's name must be unique on the sheet, comparing without regard to case and ignoring
spaces before and after the name. Names are stored with those surrounding spaces removed and
shown that way. Adding or editing a person to a name already in use is refused with an error on
the form, and nothing is saved.

agent.result_text:
Person names are now unique on each sheet, ignoring case and spaces before or after the name, and the acceptance test passes under `bin/e2e`.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V4__person_name_unique.sql`, trims names already stored. It adds a `name_key` column holding the lowercased name, with a unique index on sheet plus `name_key`. The database itself then refuses a duplicate, even if two users save the same name at the same moment.
- **Server:** `PersonService` trims the name before saving, both when adding and editing a person. It checks first whether another person on the sheet already has that name, case-insensitively and leaving out the person being edited. If so, it throws a new `NameInUseException`. `PersonController` turns that, and the database's unique-index rejection, into a 409 Conflict response, so nothing is saved.
- **Front end (`people.ts`):** the name is trimmed before it is sent. A 409 shows "Another person on the sheet is already named …" in the existing `person-form-error` element. A refused edit leaves the editor open, as the testing rules require.

The migration will fail on a database that already holds two names on one sheet differing only in case or spacing. That can't happen with this app's in-memory database, which starts empty on every run, but it would matter against stored data. In that case the duplicates would need renaming first.
